newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers due to set 'spy-in-the-cab' rules.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers due to set 'spy-in-the-cab' rules.

text.p: European Union truck drivers intent on breaking speed limits or rules on the hours they spend behind the wheel will have to contend with a digital "spy-in- the-cab" if transport ministers agree EU rules on tachographs next Tuesday.
Ministers meeting in Luxembourg will discuss a proposal which would have the new-style device fitted in all new trucks and coaches from July 2000.
The proposal would set rules for the construction, installation, use and checking of electronic tachographs, intended to replace an existing system seen as easy to fiddle.
While a majority of the EU's 15 countries favour the fixing of digital tachographs on new vehicles, divisions remain about whether old vehicles should retrofit the new technology.

One EU diplomat said ministers might drop the retrofit option, opposed by Belgium, Greece, Spain, Ireland, Italy, Portugal and Sweden, if its inclusion threatened to block a deal on the overall package.
